This Porsche Carrera GT got away, but there are more like it here.

Fayence Yellow 2005 Porsche Carrera GT

USA
P Premium
Sold for USD $4,568,000 07/22/2026435Comments
View Result
Premium Listing
MakePorsche
ModelPorsche Carrera GT
Era2000s
OriginGerman
LocationLocated in United States

This 2005 Porsche Carrera GT is one of 1,270 examples built during a four-year production run and was delivered new to Sonnen Porsche in Mill Valley, California, as one of a believed ~44 finished in Fayence Yellow for the North American market. The car is powered by a 5.7-liter V10 paired with a six-speed manual transaxle and has dark gray leather upholstery, 19″ and 20″ center-lock alloy wheels, ceramic composite brakes, an electronically actuated rear spoiler, removable roof panels, xenon headlights, air conditioning, and a Porsche Online Pro CD stereo. The current owner purchased the car in 2026 and has since added approximately 100 miles of the 9,200 miles. This Type 980 is now offered in Atlanta, Georgia, by the seller on behalf of the current owner with a set of black leather fitted luggage, a window sticker, the owner’s manual, service records, a car cover, and a Montana title in the name of the owner’s LLC.

The Carrera GT concept car first appeared at the 2000 Paris Motor Show as an offshoot of the late-1990s LMP2000 development prototype that never came to fruition. The model entered production in 2003 with construction incorporating a carbon-fiber-reinforced plastic monocoque and subframe built by ATR Group in Italy.

The carbon-fiber body panels on this example are finished in Fayence Yellow (1C1) with matching removable roof panels. Aerodynamic elements include an undertray, a rear diffuser, and an electronically actuated rear spoiler that can also be deployed using a button on the center console. Paint protection film covers the exterior.

The forged magnesium wheels measure 19×9.5” up front and 20×12.5” at the rear and are secured by center-lock nuts that are color-coded in reference to thread direction. In 2024, they were mounted with Michelin Pilot Sport Cup 2 tires measuring 265/35 front and 335/30 rear. Pushrod-activated coilover struts are mounted inboard all around, and stopping power is provided by cross-drilled 15” ceramic composite brake rotors with Fayence Yellow six-piston monobloc aluminum calipers at each corner. The brake pressure accumulator was replaced in 2023, and a suspension recall campaign was addressed in September 2024 and included replacing the front and rear wishbones, trailing arms, and associated hardware.

The cockpit features racing-style seats with carbon-fiber and Kevlar shells trimmed in dark gray leather along with a matching dashboard, center console, door A-pillars, and door caps. The Carrera GT features magnesium, carbon-fiber, and aluminum interior trim, and additional equipment includes one-touch power windows, air conditioning, heated power-adjustable side mirrors, and a Porsche Online Pro CD stereo. The high-mounted shifter is topped with a laminated beechwood knob in homage to the balsa units that appeared in Porsche 917 race cars.

The serialization ahead of the shifter denotes this chassis as #0644.

The leather-wrapped airbag steering wheel frames a central tachometer with an 8,400-rpm redline as well as a 235-mph speedometer and auxiliary gauges. The digital odometer indicates 9,200 miles, approximately 100 of which were added under current ownership.

The mid-mounted 5.7-liter M80/01 V10 is liquid-cooled and features dual overhead camshafts on each cylinder bank, titanium connecting rods, dry-sump lubrication, and Bosch Motronic ME7 engine management. It produced 605 horsepower at 8,000 rpm and 435 lb-ft of torque at 5,750 rpm when new. The car is said to be fitted with a GRP exhaust system. The drive belts were replaced in 2021, and the battery was replaced in September 2024.

Power is sent to the rear wheels through a six-speed manual transaxle and a limited-slip differential.

A set of black leather fitted luggage is included in the sale.

The window sticker shows delivery to Sonnen Porsche, factory Fayence Yellow paint, and a total price of $448,300.

@JHBBII wrote “At a traditional auction house, a big hammer price means a brutal 10% buyer’s premium with absolutely no cap”

Often, though not always, a similar fee is charged to the seller so a car that sells for slightly less at a traditional auction house may cost the buyer much more than on BaT. Even if it sells for slightly more at the traditional auction house the seller may net less. Not a pretty picture, is it?

On the other hand, a slightly higher bid on BaT than at a traditional auction house may still cost the buyer less. What’s not to love about BaT’s fee structure?

@Geh13 wrote “The way I remember it RM set the 3m mark on these cars last year.”

You may be thinking of this $3,085,000 car from 01/23/2026:
https://rmsothebys.com/auctions/az26/lots/r0048-2005-porsche-carrera-gt/

@boaboyoz wrote “11 days to go, and this superstar Carrera GT is already the new BaT Porsche result record….”

Howdy my friend, but no. So far it has set the high bid mark only. Now it has to sell to set the sold record, you know, the record that matters. Btw, the current BaT Porsche sold record was set on 01/19/2026 by a 2k-Mile 2015 Porsche 918 Spyder Weissach Package that sold for $3,205,000.

@Geh13 wrote “My other favorite BAT commentators are “S n P 500” ones. I could name 2 dozen cars off the the top of my head that if you bought right in the the mid 2000s you would be well ahead.”

I agree. Sometimes it is lost in the commentary that some wealthy people finance their cars and then put their money to work in investments that earn returns far above their borrowing costs. I commented on this on a 918 auction with an example. You can see that comment via the link below:
https://bringatrailer.com/listing/2015-porsche-918-spyder-24/#comment-19908776

Often the S&P 500 comments just take the price when new and compare that to the stock market return ignoring the buyers in between who may have seen a mix of wins and losses.
